import json, re
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

print('=== parquet schema ===')
t = pq.read_table('/app/merged_users.parquet')
print(t.schema)

df = pd.read_parquet('/app/merged_users.parquet')
print('\n=== df dtypes ===')
print(df.dtypes)
print('\n=== data ===')
print(df.to_string())

# checks
assert list(df.columns) == ['user_id', 'name', 'email', 'created_date', 'status'], df.columns
assert len(df) == df['user_id'].nunique() == 4
assert set(df['user_id']) == {101, 102, 103, 104}
assert df['user_id'].apply(lambda x: isinstance(x, int)).all()
assert df['created_date'].apply(lambda s: isinstance(s, str) and bool(re.fullmatch(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', s))).all()
assert not df['name'].isna().any() and not df['email'].isna().any()
assert not df['created_date'].isna().any() and not df['status'].isna().any()
# priority check: user 101 must come from source_a
r101 = df[df['user_id'] == 101].iloc[0]
assert r101['name'] == 'John Doe' and r101['email'] == 'john@a.com' and r101['created_date'] == '2024-01-15' and r101['status'] == 'active'
# 102 only in a, 103 only in b, 104 only in c
assert df[df['user_id']==102].iloc[0]['email'] == 'jane@a.com'
assert df[df['user_id']==103].iloc[0]['email'] == 'bob@b.com'
assert df[df['user_id']==104].iloc[0]['email'] == 'alice@c.com'

rep = json.load(open('/app/conflicts.json'))
assert rep['total_conflicts'] == len(rep['conflicts']) == 3
for c in rep['conflicts']:
    assert set(c.keys()) == {'user_id', 'field', 'values', 'selected'}
    assert set(c['values'].keys()) == {'source_a', 'source_b', 'source_c'}
    assert c['user_id'] == 101
    # selected must equal the highest-priority present value
    for s in ('source_a', 'source_b', 'source_c'):
        if c['values'][s] is not None:
            assert c['selected'] == c['values'][s], (c, s)
            break
assert {(c['field'], c['selected']) for c in rep['conflicts']} == {
    ('name', 'John Doe'), ('email', 'john@a.com'), ('created_date', '2024-01-15')}

print('\nALL CHECKS PASSED')
